# The primitive catalogue

Thirty React components with strict prop schemas — the closed vocabulary the agent
composes a task surface from. A projection block names a `type`; if the name is not
in this table the block does not exist, and there is no path from model output to the
DOM that avoids that check.

Every primitive has **four states**: `ready`, `empty` (its data is present and has
nothing in it), `loading` (`state: "loading"`) and `error` (`state: "error"` plus
`error`). Every one renders on both grounds from `tokens.css`, is reachable by
keyboard through real `<button>` and `<a>` elements, carries no `box-shadow` on
content, and takes its radii from {6, 8, 10}. **No primitive accepts raw HTML except
Preview**, which renders in a sandboxed iframe.

See [composition.md](composition.md) for the projection schema and the six personas,
and `/gallery` (served by `gear serve --web`, linked from nowhere in the product) for
all thirty in every state on both grounds.

## The base props

Spread into every primitive's schema, flat rather than nested, because a projection
block's props are flat on the wire:

| prop    | type                                         | meaning                                     |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `label` | `string?`                                    | the accessible name and the visible eyebrow |
| `state` | `"ready" \| "loading" \| "error"` (optional) | the block's LOAD state                      |
| `error` | `string?`                                    | what failed, shown in the error state       |

It is `state` and not `status` deliberately: four primitives have a domain status of
their own — a hypothesis is `refuted`, an agent is `working` — and P11.1 names that
field `status` on the task state, so a base key called `status` would overwrite a
verdict with a load state on every one of them.

## Binding

`bind` on a block resolves a dotted state path; how the value becomes props is the
primitive's own `bind.mode`:

| mode     | what happens                                                               |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `assign` | `props[key] = value` — a list into `rows`, `items`, `points`               |
| `merge`  | `props = { …props, …value }` — an object of fields                         |
| `repeat` | one component per array element, the element spread over the block's props |
| `none`   | the primitive takes no live data                                           |

`foldable` marks the primitives that honour a `folded` prop, which is what lets
`foldWhen` be a closed predicate rather than a callback. `interactive` marks the ones
that take callbacks the projection cannot supply; the shell wires those.

| ------- | --------------------------------- | -------- |
| `label` | `string`                          | optional |
| `state` | `"ready" \| "loading" \| "error"` | optional |
| `error` | `string`                          | optional |
| `body`  | `string`                          | required |
| `muted` | `boolean`                         | optional |
